symptom: A JSON payload with a member named `owner`, `class`, `int`, `changedDate` or any other Java keyword makes `create json structure` produce a project mxbuild REFUSES to build: **CE9524** "JSON element '(Object)/owner' has an invalid custom name 'Owner'. Custom name should start with a letter or underscore followed by either letters, digits or underscores."
cause: `resolveExposedName` prefixes an underscore for names Mendix reserves — Studio Pro's own scheme, keeping the key's ORIGINAL case (`_id`, `_object` in OpenAI_API.JSON_OpenAI_Response) — but the list held only `{Id, Type}`. Every other reserved name went through capitalised and was rejected at build time, with nothing before that warning: `mxcli check` passes and `exec` succeeds
insight: **Do not trust the CE message to name its own rule** — 'Owner' matches the character pattern it quotes perfectly. Probe instead: one structure per candidate name, one `mx check`, read the rejected list off the output. Measured on mxbuild 11.13: **53 Java keywords and literals**, the four system attribute names (Owner/ChangedDate/CreatedDate/ChangedBy), plus CurrentUser and Guid. It is **not** the entity-member reserved list — `Type` and `Id` are ACCEPTED here (they stay in the map only because Studio Pro avoids them, which is why the list is "what Studio Pro avoids", a superset of "what mxbuild rejects"). Match **case-insensitively**: Mendix's check is, since `class` derives `Class`, which is not literally a keyword and is still rejected. The author cannot rename a member of an external payload, so deriving a valid name is the only fix — refusing at check time would make the construct unusable. A customNameMap entry still wins, so a structure read back from a project keeps the name it already carries. Repro: `create json structure X snippet '{"owner": "o"}'`, then `mx check`. Tests `mdl/types/json_exposed_name_test.go`. Issue ako/mxcli#300
